decisions.reason: The independent upper-tower rigidity clause from message 173 is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; underside serviceability adds no further structural-stability change.
Underside maintenance access does not change the strategy of using off-the-shelf electronic components.
The positive comments about the integrated form factor are praise, while the underside-serviceability requirement does not necessarily alter the accepted bulkier enclosure form.
Accessibility for future maintenance does not change the existing leak-free seal requirements.
Message 173 reiterates concern about splash control at higher RPMs, which is already present in the candidate state, and the underside-serviceability change adds no new splash constraint.
Maintenance accessibility does not modify the requirement that liquid remain isolated from electrical components.
The favorable description of the curved tower and spout does not establish a new geometry or orientation value, and underside serviceability does not necessarily change the spout configuration.
The source discusses physical integration and future maintenance access but does not request a change to the system-layout or CAD deliverable.
The source's cleaning and sanitation concern does not replace or modify the existing removable, easy-to-clean spout method; the separate underside-access change concerns future maintenance.
The source does not require a new component, revise a selected component, or reopen the finalized BOM to provide underside access.
Underside serviceability does not change the dispensing control mechanism, sequence, flow behavior, or operator controls.
The source's maintenance-access change does not modify mixing quality, foam performance, whisk selection, positioning, or high-speed mixing behavior.
